caption: The drawing consists of two adjacent estate plans rendered in watercolor and ink. The left side (depicting the "Mrs. Geo. J.S. Thompson Estate") is dominated by soft greens, with a circular driveway encircling a reddish-roofed, angular building, surrounded by trees, patches of shrubs, and two blue circular features near the building, likely representing pools or fountains. The circular drive is bordered by rows of evenly spaced evergreen trees, and outside of this, a larger irregularly shaped expanse of pale green, possibly open lawn, is contained within curving white paths. The right side (labeled "Jacob Hayes Estate") has denser and more diverse color blocks, including a rectangular blue area resembling a swimming pool, irregular green shrubbery, and varied round forms in oranges, reds, and yellows suggesting trees or garden beds. The paths in this area are shaded in pinkish brown and dark brown, winding through a grid-like arrangement of circular red and brown objects. Both estates are labeled in blue text in the lower right. The name "THE BLACKWELL SURVEY" appears at the bottom, with the numbers "25" and "50" on either side. The background of the drawing is a light beige color.
title: Hayes and Thompson Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
